vo.hook: We didn't ask experts. We ran 1,000 simulated families through 10 years of real US housing data. Half rented. Half bought. The results broke almost every rule you've heard.
vo.setup: Same income. Same city. One family rented and invested the difference every single month. The other bought a $300,000 home and stayed for a decade. 10 years of real market data. Who built more wealth?
vo.tension: Everyone assumed the buyer crushed it. And in most markets — they did come out ahead. But here's the part nobody talks about. The families who bought and sold before year 5? Almost every one of them lost money. Realtor fees, closing costs, property taxes, and maintenance wiped out their gains completely.
vo.reveal: In a moderate US market, after 10 years, the buyer netted around $89,000 in real wealth — equity minus every cost. The renter who actually invested the gap every month? $73,000. A $16,000 difference. Over a decade. That is the entire rent versus buy debate right there.
vo.twist: Buyer wins. But barely. And only if they stayed the full 10 years and invested nothing extra. The renter who showed up every month and invested the difference came within $16,000. In a flat market, that renter won outright. The question was never rent or buy. It was — what is your plan, and can you actually stick to it? Run your own numbers free at the link below. Comment the word RENT and I will send you the full breakdown.

disclaimer: Simulation only — not financial advice. Numbers vary by market, timeline, and investment behavior. Speak to a licensed advisor for your situation.
